QUOTE: Struct fields are declared as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)`, so by default a field `foo` is actually named `private_foo`. Code outside the library that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile... It is a compile-time guard, not an access-control mechanism.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that opacity is enforced at compile time by renaming members to `private_foo`, not by hiding the struct. It does not say outright that the fields stay visible and sized, but it implies this: the same macro produces the mangled name and the code still compiles.
